name: Luminal Digestion, Brush-Border Hydrolases, Enterocyte Transport, and Malabsorption

reference.source: Medical Biochemistry 5th ed / Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd ed
clinicalPearls: Glucose and galactose are actively absorbed via apical SGLT1 driven by the Na+/K+-ATPase gradient; exit is via GLUT2
Fructose is absorbed independently via facilitated diffusion mediated by apical GLUT5 transporters
Lipid absorption requires mixed bile salt micelles delivering 2-MAG and FFAs for re-esterification into chylomicrons
Celiac disease is triggered by dietary gluten, causing anti-tTG IgA elevation, duodenal villous atrophy, and malabsorption
Abetalipoproteinemia is an MTTP deficiency preventing Apo B-48/B-100 assembly, causing fat-stuffed enterocytes and acanthocytes
reference.pathophysiology: Dietary macromolecules require luminal enzymatic cleavage followed by enterocyte microvillar hydrolysis and carrier transport. In celiac disease, deamidated gliadin peptides provoke an HLA-DQ2/DQ8 restricted T-cell response, causing enterocyte apoptosis, villous blunting, and secondary disaccharidase and nutrient loss. In abetalipoproteinemia, failure of microsomal triglyceride transfer protein halts chylomicron and VLDL export, trapping neutral lipids within enterocytes.
additionalDifferentials: Exocrine pancreatic insufficiency (chronic pancreatitis, cystic fibrosis)
additionalInvestigations: Serum anti-tissue transglutaminase (anti-tTG) IgA antibody and total serum IgA level
Upper endoscopy with multiple oriented duodenal bulb and distal duodenal biopsies
Fecal fat quantification (72-hour collection) and fecal elastase-1 (exocrine pancreas)
Peripheral blood smear examination for acanthocytes (spurred red cells) and lipid panel
